question: Is Krabbe disease inherited ?
references: This condition is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, which means both copies of the gene in each cell have mutations. The parents of an individual with an autosomal recessive condition each carry one copy of the mutated gene, but they typically do not show signs and symptoms of the condition.

Yes, Krabbe disease is an inherited disorder. It is a rare genetic disorder caused by a deficiency of the enzyme galactocerebrosidase (GALC), which is necessary for the breakdown of certain fatty substances in the brain and spinal cord.

Krabbe disease is inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern, which means that a person must inherit two copies of the mutated gene (one from each parent) to develop the disease. Carriers of the mutated gene, who have one normal and one mutated copy, are usually asymptomatic but can pass the mutated gene to their offspring.

The mutated gene responsible for Krabbe disease is located on chromosome 14 and is called GALC. When both parents are carriers of the mutated gene, there is a 25% chance that each child will inherit two copies of the mutated gene (one from each parent) and develop the disease, a 50% chance that each child will inherit one copy of the mutated gene and be a carrier, and a 25% chance that each child will inherit two normal copies of the gene and not be affected.

Krabbe disease can also occur spontaneously in some cases, without a family history of the disease, due to a new mutation in the GALC gene.
